newsitem.title: USA: US sets California payment plan on Elk Hills share.
newsitem.headline: US sets California payment plan on Elk Hills share.

text.p: The U.S. Energy Department agreed Thursday to pay the state of California its 9 percent share of the proceeds from the sale of the Elk Hills Naval Petroleum Reserve in five installments beginning in 1999.
Under law, the U.S. government must sell its majority stake in the Elk Hills oil and gas field in Bakersfield, California, by February 1998.

The law included a provision to give the California teachers pension fund 9 percent of the sale revenue to settle a decades old dispute between the federal government and the state over some of the Elk Hills land.

Under Thursday's agreement, the Energy Department would pay the state its share, up to $180 million, in five equal parts from 1999 through 2003. Any amount above $180 million would be paid out in two equal installemtns in 2004 and 2005.

"If Congress does not fund the settlement, or funds only part of the settlement, the state may terminate the agreement and sue DOE (the Energy Department) or the purchasers for damages," the Energy Department said.
However the state may not block a sale of the field.
